Rashi on Menachot 80a:1:1.english: Rather, this refers to the exchange of a thanksgiving-offering for a freewill-offering: for it says, "This is hereby [so-and-so], and it was lost, and he sets aside another in its place" — meaning, this refers to the end of that baraita, which states, "From where do we know [the law of] substitution and exchange?" which is taught in unspecified terms, and it teaches us [that this applies] to the exchange of a thanksgiving-offering for a freewill-offering. And Rabbi Yochanan said about it: "They only taught this... etc."

Rashi on Menachot 80a:1:2.english: "Whether before atonement or after atonement" - meaning: he achieved atonement through the other [thanksgiving-offering], both of them require bread, because he is considered one who increases thanksgiving-offerings. Since he was not obligated to set aside another one, and yet he set it aside anyway, he revealed his intention that he meant to add more voluntary thanksgiving-offerings; therefore he brings bread with each of their loaves.

Rashi on Menachot 80a:2:1.english: Rather, the offspring of a voluntary thanks-offering - For example, one set aside an animal [as a thanks-offering] and it gave birth: whether he sacrifices [the offspring] before achieving atonement or after achieving atonement, it does not require bread, because it is a leftover of the thanks-offering, since he already achieved atonement with the other [animal] — comparable to one who set aside money for his thanks-offering and had money left over. For anything that comes about on its own, such as offspring, is considered a leftover:

Rashi on Menachot 80a:2:2.hebrew: אלא אוולד תודת חובה - וכי קתני לעיל ולא ולדה טעון לחם לאחר כפרה, אבל לפני כפרה טעון? והתם ליכא למיפרך בין לפני וכו', מרבה בתודות הוא, דאין אדם מרבה בתודת חובה:
Rashi on Menachot 80a:2:2.english: Rather, the offspring of an obligatory thanksgiving-offering - But is this not taught above, that its offspring does not require bread after atonement, but before atonement it does require bread? And there one cannot raise the objection "whether before... etc.," since that case is one of increasing thanksgiving-offerings, whereas a person does not increase an obligatory thanksgiving-offering.

Rashi on Menachot 80a:3:1.hebrew: אדם מתכפר בשבח הקדש - דהיינו הולד [של תודת חובה], וכיון דיכול להתכפר באיזו שירצה, או באם או בולד, הכי נמי טעונות לחם:
Rashi on Menachot 80a:3:1.english: A person is atoned for through the increase of the consecrated animal - meaning the offspring [of an obligatory thanksgiving offering]. And since he may be atoned for with whichever one he wishes, either with the mother or with the offspring, so too both of them require bread.

Rashi on Menachot 80a:3:2.english: Abaye also raised this same difficulty - Concerning what [statement did he raise it], and how did he resolve it? Concerning the offspring of an obligatory thanksgiving-offering.

Tosafot on Menachot 80a:3:1.hebrew: מאי קמשמע לן דקסבר רבי יוחנן מתכפר אדם בשבח הקדש - משמע הכא דפשיטא לן דאית ליה לרבי יוחנן הך סברא, וכן משמע נמי בפרק בתרא דכריתות (דף כז.) דבעי רבי אלעזר: אדם מתכפר בשבח הקדש או לא? אמר רבי יוחנן: כמה שנים גדל זה בינינו ולא שמע הלכה זו ממנו! מכלל דאמרה ר' יוחנן. אין, ועל הדא אמרה, דתנן: וולד תודה ותמורתה כו', ומייתי הך דשמעתין. ותימה, דבתמורה בפ' כיצד מערימין (תמורה דף כה.) אמר רבי יוחנן: הפריש חטאת מעוברת וילדה, רצה בה מתכפר, רצה בוולדה מתכפר. מאי טעמא? קסבר ר' יוחנן: אם שיירה משוייר, עובר לאו ירך אמו הוא, והוה ליה כמפריש שתי חטאות לאחריות, רצה בה מתכפר, רצה בחברתה. ומותיב התם ר' אלעזר, ומסיק כתנאי. ופריך רבא: ממאי דטעמא דר' יוחנן דאם שיירו משוייר? דלמא היינו טעמא דרבי יוחנן, דאדם מתכפר בשבח הקדש! א"ל רב המנונא: מכדי רבי אלעזר תלמידיה דר' יוחנן, ויתיב קמיה דר' יוחנן ולא אהדר ליה האי שינויא, ואת אמרת טעמא דר' יוחנן משום דאדם מתכפר בשבח הקדש? נראה לפרש, דדווקא בחטאת צריך לומר טעמא משום דאם שיירו משוייר, דאם איתא דאינו משוייר משום דעובר ירך אמו, לא היה מתכפר בשבח הקדש, משום דקיימא לן (מעילה דף י:) חמש חטאות מתות, ולד חטאת כו'. אבל השתא דעובר לאו ירך אמו הוא, מתכפר בולד, כבשתי חטאות לאחריות דמי. והא דקיימא לן ולד חטאת מתה, מיתוקמא בהפרישה ואח"כ נתעברה. אבל בולד תודה, מתכפר אפי' הפרישה ואח"כ נתעברה, דאדם מתכפר בשבח הקדש, כדאיתא הכא ובכריתות (דף כז.). ומתיישבת בכך שמעתא דבסמוך, אמר שמואל: כל שבחטאת מתה, בתודה אין טעון לחם. ומסיק: שמואל כר"ש סבירא ליה, דאמר חמש חטאות מתות ורועה, לר"ש לית ליה כלל. ושמואל מאי קמשמע לן? לאפוקי מדרבי יוחנן, הא שפיר אית ליה לרבי יוחנן נמי האי כללא, דאם אדם מתכפר בשבח הקדש בתודה, הכי נמי מתכפר בשבח הקדש בחטאת, ואינה מתה בחטאת, ולכך טעונה לחם כתודה. אלא ודאי בחטאת אין מתכפר בשבח הקדש, דאי כשהפריש חטאת מעוברת, ההוא לא מיקרי שבח הקדש לר' יוחנן, כיון דלאו ירך אמו הוא, דאם שיירו משוייר, דהוה ליה כמפריש שתי חטאות לאחריות. ואי בהפרישה ואחר כך נתעברה, הוה ליה ולד חטאת מתה ואין מתכפר בה. וכיוצא בה בתודת חובה, טעונה לחם, דמתכפר בשבח הקדש. ומיהו קצת קשה, דלקמן גבי מפריש חטאת מעוברת מסיק דלמא אם שיירו משוייר, וטעמא דר' יוחנן דקסבר אדם מתכפר בשבח הקדש:
Tosafot on Menachot 80a:3:1.english: What does this come to teach us, that Rabbi Yoḥanan holds that a person is atoned for through the enhancement of consecrated property - This implies here that it is obvious to us that Rabbi Yoḥanan holds this view. And so it also implies in the last chapter of Keritot (27a), where Rabbi Elazar asked: is a person atoned for through the enhancement of consecrated property, or not? Rabbi Yoḥanan replied: "How many years has this one grown up among us, and never heard this halakha from me!" - implying that Rabbi Yoḥanan did indeed say it. Yes, and it was in reference to this that he said it, for we learned: "the offspring of a thanks-offering and its substitute," etc. - and it cites this same passage of our sugya. But this is difficult: for in Temurah, in the chapter "How Does One Act with Cunning" (25a), Rabbi Yoḥanan says: one who set aside a pregnant sin-offering and it gave birth - if he wishes, he is atoned for through it, and if he wishes, he is atoned for through its offspring. What is the reason? Rabbi Yoḥanan holds that if he reserved it, the reservation is effective - an embryo is not [legally considered] its mother's limb - so it is as though he had set aside two sin-offerings as a guarantee for each other (in case one is lost): if he wishes, he is atoned for through this one, if he wishes, through its counterpart. Rabbi Elazar raises an objection there, and the Gemara concludes that it is a dispute among tanna'im. Rava then asks: how do we know that Rabbi Yoḥanan's reasoning is that the reservation is effective? Perhaps Rabbi Yoḥanan's reasoning is rather that a person is atoned for through the enhancement of consecrated property! Rav Hamnuna said to him: now, Rabbi Elazar was Rabbi Yoḥanan's disciple and sat before him, and Rabbi Yoḥanan did not give him this answer [when he raised his objection] - yet you say Rabbi Yoḥanan's reasoning is that a person is atoned for through the enhancement of consecrated property? It seems that the explanation is that specifically regarding a sin-offering, it is necessary to give the reason that a reservation, if made, is effective. For if it were not effective - because an embryo is considered its mother's limb - one would not be atoned for through the enhancement of consecrated property, since we hold (Me'ilah 10b) that there are five sin-offerings that must die, [among them] the offspring of a sin-offering, etc. But now that an embryo is not its mother's limb, one is atoned for through the offspring, since it is considered like two sin-offerings set aside as a guarantee. And the ruling that the offspring of a sin-offering must die refers to a case where he set the animal aside [as a sin-offering] and it became pregnant only afterward. But regarding the offspring of a thanks-offering, one is atoned for even when he set it aside and it became pregnant afterward, because a person is atoned for through the enhancement of consecrated property, as stated both here and in Keritot (27a). This also resolves the passage shortly afterward, where Shmuel says: whatever, in the case of a sin-offering, must die - in the case of a thanks-offering, does not require bread. And the Gemara concludes that Shmuel holds like Rabbi Shimon, who says there are five sin-offerings that must die, and that Rabbi Shimon does not accept the option of grazing [until blemished] at all. And what does Shmuel come to teach us? To exclude a mistaken inference from Rabbi Yoḥanan's ruling - one might have thought that Rabbi Yoḥanan indeed accepts this general principle as well: that just as a person is atoned for through the enhancement of consecrated property in the case of a thanks-offering, so too he would be atoned for through the enhancement of consecrated property in the case of a sin-offering, and it would not have to die in the case of a sin-offering, and would therefore require bread like a thanks-offering. Rather, [Shmuel teaches] that, certainly, in the case of a sin-offering one is not atoned for through the enhancement of consecrated property. For when he set aside a pregnant sin-offering, that is not called "the enhancement of consecrated property" according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, since the embryo is not its mother's limb - for if he reserved it, the reservation is effective - so that it is as though he set aside two sin-offerings as a guarantee. And if it became pregnant after he had set the animal aside, then it is a case of "the offspring of a sin-offering that must die," and he is not atoned for through it. Whereas in the corresponding case with an obligatory thanks-offering, [the offspring] requires bread, because one is atoned for through the enhancement of consecrated property. However, it is somewhat difficult: for further on, regarding one who sets aside a pregnant sin-offering, the Gemara raises the possibility that perhaps it is not that the reservation is effective, but rather that Rabbi Yoḥanan's reasoning is that he holds a person is atoned for through the enhancement of consecrated property.
